-v, -remote, -local-only and -allow-upgrade choose the IPM version and where it comes from.
obligations.cases: each flag vs default source/version

obligations.gap: No model of version/source selection in Main.cls::EnableIPM. Contrast: `enable -ns NS2 -v 0.10.1 -local-only` installs 0.10.1 from the local package, vs -remote fetching the registry version.

obligations.text: -preview makes no changes.
-preview shows the changes it would make.
obligations.cases: preview vs real run
obligations.observation: printed plan matches the real run's changes
obligations.gap: Preview output is not modeled; request(..., preview) only returns the unchanged state. Contrast: the preview listing for NS2 names the same mappings a real run then creates.

obligations.text: -community sets up the community registry and maps IPM and its repositories to all namespaces, like IPM 0.7.
obligations.cases: empty targets vs targets already reaching the code; source registry state before
obligations.observation: registry rows of the source; code and repositories each namespace uses
obligations.gap: nsp_lemma_community proves the L1 effect only under premise REPOS (every non-local target already reaches IPM code). For an empty target the same enable_map first pass leaves repositories local (F-NSP-4 witness for enable_map), and no witness exercises community on such a target. The registry is abstracted to "rows present" (reset_repos), not the community URL. Contrast: `enable -community` on an instance with an empty NS2: NS2 runs USER's code but reads its own (empty) repositories after one run.

obligations.text: Working assumption: the source of a mapped namespace is the namespace whose own code database holds the IPM code.
obligations.cases: single source vs two zpm records reaching one code database
obligations.observation: which source GetMapInfo assigns to a target
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (F-NSP-7 witness: a later-named namespace with its own zpm record that maps USER's database wins the tie; open question namespace.enable.source-ambiguity-policy)

obligations.text: Working assumption: if a step of enable -community fails, the command stops and returns that error.
obligations.cases: repo -delete-all / -reset-defaults / enable step fails vs all succeed
obligations.observation: returned status; later steps run or not
obligations.gap: ns_mapping.rs has no success/failure result for any command (header). Contrast: a failing `repo -reset-defaults` step inside `enable -community` returns its error and no namespace is mapped, vs success. Open question namespace.enable.community-failure-policy.
